lines: Water control shaped human civilization for millennia.
Societies mastering it thrived; others collapsed entirely.
Today seven in ten have running water.
Yet this security hides deeper vulnerabilities ahead.
Cape Town faces Day Zero very soon.
Four million residents will lose tap water.
They'll queue at stations for rationed supplies.
Modern infrastructure cannot guarantee water security anymore.
Cape Town is not alone in danger.
São Paulo, Melbourne, Jakarta, London face crises.
Beijing, Istanbul, Tokyo, Bangalore will too soon.
By 2040, most lack sufficient yearly water.
Earth holds 326 million trillion gallons total.
Yet ninety-seven percent is saltwater only.
Two percent freezes at the polar caps.
One percent remains for all human survival.
Mexico City exemplifies catastrophic water mismanagement clearly.
Spanish colonizers drained the Aztec lakes centuries ago.
Now the city floods despite London-level rainfall.
Distant pipes and aquifers sustain four million.
Aquifer extraction depletes faster than natural refill.
Half the city's water comes from underground.
Supply could vanish within thirty to fifty years.
Soil compression sinks the city nine inches annually.
Agriculture and industry consume vastly more water.
One hamburger requires 1,650 liters to produce.
A cotton shirt needs 2,500 liters total.
Meat-heavy diets make water demand unsustainable globally.
Water pricing stays artificially low everywhere today.
Farmers pay almost nothing for their supply.
Southern California grows desert alfalfa below cost.
True pricing could redirect agriculture toward sustainability.
